headline: Fix one number, squeeze the remaining pair
statement: Find every distinct value triplet in nums whose sum is zero. Three different array positions must supply each triplet; the returned triplets may appear in any order.
intuition: Sort the numbers so that larger values are to the right. Choose one number, then look for the other two using pointers at opposite ends of the remaining part. If the total is too small, move the left pointer. If it is too large, move the right pointer.
approach: Sort a copy of the input.
Choose each distinct first value, stopping when it becomes positive.
Move left and right toward each other, guided by the sum.
On zero, record the triplet and skip equal neighbors on both sides.
correctness: For a fixed first value, a sum below zero rules out every pair using that left value with a smaller right value. A sum above zero similarly rules out that right value with a larger left value. Therefore pointer movements cannot skip a solution. Distinct anchors and duplicate skipping emit each value triplet exactly once.
bruteForce: Try all index triples in O(n^3) time, then deduplicate their sorted values. Sorting exposes monotonic choices and reduces the search to O(n^2).

complexity.explanation: Sorting uses a copied array; each anchor scans the remaining range once.

pitfalls: Skip duplicate anchors as well as duplicate pairs.
Use three different positions even when values repeat.
Return all triplets, not the first match.
